notes: The five LED/resistor branches differ in breadboard column and Arduino pin, so they are written out explicitly rather than as a repeat.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention (upper half = bank 't', rows a-e; lower half = bank 'b', rows f-j). The image labels rows in the opposite order, so the resistor legs sit in the rows next to the centre gap (t.e and b.f), and the LED legs and blue wires sit further out.

The longer, bent LED leg is taken as the anode (A). It shares a column with the resistor's upper leg. The cathode (C) is in the next column and is wired to the top negative rail by a short black jumper.
Rail hole numbers (tn.N) are approximate. Any hole on the same rail strip is electrically identical.
The ground wire goes from the Uno GND pin beside AREF (GND.1) to the top negative rail.

The 220 ohm value comes from the schematic and the parts list. Pin mapping: pin 6 -> LED1, 5 -> LED2, 4 -> LED3, 3 -> LED4, 2 -> LED5. The USB cable to the computer is not drawn in the circuit image, so it is omitted.
